age.evidence: Male Sprague Dawley rats (approximately 250-300 g body weight)

dosing.evidence: psilocybin (0.5 mg/kg SC) cue... psilocybin (0.1-3 mg/kg SC)... following oral administration

dosing.doses_raw: 0.1-3 mg/kg SC; oral doses up to 6 mg/kg
dosing.evidence: 5-MeO-DMT (1 mg/kg SC) cue... 5-MeO-DMT (0.1-3 mg/kg SC)... oral doses up to 6 mg/kg

assays.assay_description: Two-lever operant chambers (Med Associates); rats trained on FR10 to discriminate psilocybin (0.5 mg/kg SC) or 5-MeO-DMT (1 mg/kg SC) from saline. Test sessions up to 30 min or 50 pellets. Outcomes: % drug-appropriate lever responding and response rate. Tests included substitution/generalisation, antagonism, and time-course at varied pre-treatment times (10 min – 24 h).

application_type.evidence: Training drugs and substituted drugs given SC or orally; antagonists given IP

setup_habituation.evidence: Initial training to lever press described, but pre-test apparatus habituation not explicitly described

setup_restrain.evidence: Med Associates standard operant test chambers; freely moving lever pressing

food_restriction.evidence: All rats were singly housed and food restricted to ~20 g food/day

time_to_assay.evidence: Typically, these timepoints were 10 min, 30 min, 1, 2, 4 and 8 h... Some generalisation (12%) was noted in rats 24 h post-treatment

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin and 5-MeO-DMT engendered reliable stimulus control. 5-HT2A antagonist M100907 selectively attenuated the psilocybin cue; 5-HT1A antagonist WAY100635 selectively blocked the 5-MeO-DMT cue. DMT, LSD and 25I-NBOMe fully generalised to psilocybin; 8-OH-DPAT and lisuride fully generalised to 5-MeO-DMT. Time-course showed rank-order LSD > psilocybin > 5-MeO-DMT ≈ DMT for duration of drug-lever generalisation. Plasma psilocin levels (~5–52 ng/mL) overlapped clinical exposures; LSD showed PK/PD disconnect.
outcomes.statistics: * p < 0.05 versus vehicle (specific test statistics not reported in text)
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin fully generalised to its cue... LSD produced a dose-related generalisation to both cue types... LSD > psilocybin > 5-MeO-DMT ≧ DMT

B1_num_measures.evidence: mean percentage of responses on the drug-appropriate lever... Response rate was expressed as a function of the number of responses made divided by the total session time

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Data expressed as overall % drug-appropriate responding over the total session; no within-session time-bin analysis

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of behavioural sequences or transitions reported

B4_ethological.evidence: Operant lever pressing is not an ethological behaviour

B5_social.evidence: Singly housed rats tested alone in operant chamber

B6_cognitive.evidence: Rats trained to discriminate a distinct interoceptive state and to associate this state with a specific behavioural response

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Med Associates standard operant test chambers controlled by Med-PC software

B8_multivariate.evidence: Percent drug-appropriate responding and response rate were graphed as a function of dose of test compound

E1_environment_type.evidence: Med Associates standard operant test chambers

E6_spatial.evidence: Standard two-lever operant chamber - single compartment

E7_social_context.evidence: Focal animal alone in operant chamber during testing

E8_food_water.evidence: every 10th response on either lever resulted in delivery of a food pellet

D1_continuity.evidence: Drug testing was conducted on Tuesdays and Fridays... Rats were only tested under one single timepoint per session; consequently, multiple test sessions were required

D2_session_duration.evidence: Training sessions lasted for a maximum of 30 min or until the delivery of 50 pellets

D3_recording_days.evidence: Training to the psilocybin cue required approximately 30-50 sessions... Drug testing conducted on Tuesdays and Fridays across multiple substitution, antagonism and time-course experiments

D4_baseline.evidence: Vehicle pre-treatment data reported (e.g. Vehicle 0.5 ± 0.2 % generalisation)

D5_followup.evidence: Some generalisation (12%) was noted in rats 24 h post-treatment [for LSD]

D6_circadian.evidence: Sessions lasted a maximum of 30 min

judge_notes: All candidates correctly identified a single drug discrimination assay (two cohorts trained to psilocybin or 5-MeO-DMT cues collapsed as one paradigm with different training drugs/manipulations).
Resolved food_restriction = 'before' (rats food-restricted to ~20 g/day to motivate operant responding) rather than 'no'; food pellets delivered during the session.
D3 set to 15+ given >30 training sessions plus numerous substitution, antagonism and time-course test sessions for this assay.
D4 set to Yes because vehicle pre-treatment generalisation data are reported in Table 2 (baseline recordings in the same assay/environment).

Expanded dosing entries to cover all administered compounds (psilocybin, 5-MeO-DMT, DMT, LSD, 2-Br LSD, lisuride, 25I-NBOMe); antagonists and other reference 5-HT agonists also administered but only the psychedelic-class compounds are listed in dosing.
Age scored 'not_reported' because only body weight is given (250–300 g); age in days/weeks not stated.
